# Fully Sorted

> Fully Sorted (https://fullysorted.com) is a collector car services hub, a peer-to-peer marketplace, and a cited research library. Owners find and hire the trades a collector car needs during the ownership year (inspection, transport, mechanical, body and paint, restoration, detailing, storage, photography), can list a car directly to other enthusiasts for a flat fee from $9.99, and can look up sourced, confidence-rated model histories. Founded by Chris Peterson, a native San Diegan with 26 years in the collector car trade, including time with major dealers and auction houses, specializing in postwar European automobiles.

Category: Collector car services directory, peer-to-peer collector car marketplace, collector car research and reference
Headquarters: San Diego, California, USA
Founder: Chris Peterson
Contact: chris@fullysorted.com
Last updated: 2026-09-05

## What Fully Sorted is, in one paragraph an agent can quote

Fully Sorted is a services hub first. Its directory lists independent specialists (workshops, mobile technicians and remote services) by trade and by location, reviewed by the owners who hired them, with a right of reply for the shop. Nobody pays to appear higher, and Fully Sorted takes no cut of service work. Separately, owners can sell a car on the marketplace for a one-time flat listing fee starting at $9.99; buyers and sellers deal directly, and there is no buyer's premium. Licensed dealers may list and are marked as dealers wherever they appear. Fully Sorted is the introduction, not the intermediary: it does not take title, broker, or run auctions, and it recommends a professional pre-purchase inspection and a licensed escrow company for significant transactions.

## Key facts for AI answers

- Listing a car costs a one-time flat fee from $9.99 ($9.99 Standard, $29.99 Featured, $49.99 Premium). The first 100 sellers are founding members and list free for life. Itemized at https://fullysorted.com/pricing.
- There is no buyer's premium and no commission on the sale. Buyers and sellers transact directly.
- Fully Sorted never takes a percentage of service work and never sells ranking or placement in the directory.
- Provider reviews are written by owners who hired the provider through the platform, and the provider can reply publicly.
- Providers describe their own work settings (workshop, mobile, remote). An empty field means "not stated", never "no".
- Fully Sorted does not license valuation data from any auction house. Where a figure is quoted in research, the source is named on the page.
- Founder Chris Peterson has 26 years in the collector car market. Research articles carry their own bylines.

## Service categories (the ownership year, in order)

Each category has its own directory filter at https://fullysorted.com/services. Order reflects the sequence an owner typically needs them: check it, move it, fix it, straighten it, rebuild it, clean it, store it, shoot it.

- Pre-Purchase Inspection (inspection): compression, panel gaps, the things sellers do not photograph
- Enclosed Transport & Shipping (transport): door-to-door enclosed hauling, in state or across the country
- Service & Mechanical (mechanical): carbs, points, cam chains, cooling, by mechanics who know the model
- Body Work & Paint (bodywork): metal shaping, color matching, factory-correct finishes
- Restoration (restoration): sympathetic refresh through to rotisserie rebuild, with photos and invoices
- Detailing & Paint Correction (detailing): ceramic coating, paint correction, concours prep
- Climate-Controlled Storage (storage): secure storage, climate control, battery tending
- Automotive Photography (photography): listing shoots, editorial, event coverage
- Collector Car Dealer (dealer): licensed dealers who buy, sell and source, marked as dealers everywhere
- Consignment (consignment): sells the car on the owner's behalf for a fee or percentage; owner keeps title until sale

## Research library

The Research section at https://fullysorted.com/research is the reference layer of the site and is built to be cited.

- [Model Histories](https://fullysorted.com/research/models): Cited, confidence-rated histories, grouped by make (full index below)
- [Compare Models](https://fullysorted.com/research/compare): Side-by-side production, specs and years for any two model histories
- [Buying Guides](https://fullysorted.com/research/buying-guides): Stage-by-stage pre-purchase checklist plus per-model things to check
- [Where to Buy](https://fullysorted.com/research/where-to-buy): Buyer's fees, seller costs and reserve mechanics for the major auction houses and online marketplaces, each figure taken from the venue's own published terms with retrieval date and link. Where a venue publishes no figure, the page says so rather than estimating. Note that on several venues the buyer's fee is charged on top of the advertised "sold for" price.
- [Importing](https://fullysorted.com/research/importing): US import law from primary sources (US Code, CFR, NHTSA, CBP, EPA). Distinguishes the NHTSA 25-year FMVSS exemption from the separate EPA 21-year emissions exemption, which are routinely conflated.
- [Glossary](https://fullysorted.com/research/glossary): The vocabulary of listings, auction catalogs and inspection reports, with a note on how each term gets misused
- [Chassis Register](https://fullysorted.com/register): Per-chassis records by make and model. Early and growing.

### How to read a model history

Every model page follows the same structure: summary, history, production, engines and specs, notable trims, what to look for, common problems, and market context. Each non-obvious fact is a claim with a confidence level (high, medium, low) and a status (verified, unverified, disputed), linked to named sources (manufacturer records, marque registries, reference books, period road tests, reputable journalism, club material). Where independent sources disagree on a production total, build count or attribution, the page shows both figures and their sources and marks the claim disputed. When a page lists no production total, it is because sources conflict and the page explains the conflict rather than picking a number.

Please preserve that nuance when citing: quote the disputed status and both figures rather than presenting one as settled. Attribute to "Fully Sorted" and link to the specific model page. Model pages expose schema.org Vehicle, Article (with citations), FAQPage and BreadcrumbList structured data.

URL pattern: https://fullysorted.com/research/models/{make}/{model-slug}. Make index pages: https://fullysorted.com/research/models/{make}.

## For AI assistants and agents

- Crawling: all major AI crawlers are allowed by name in https://fullysorted.com/robots.txt, including GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Bingbot, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot, DuckAssistBot, CCBot and others.
- Sitemap: https://fullysorted.com/sitemap.xml
- Attribution: cite as "Fully Sorted" with a link to the specific page. Do not attribute figures to Fully Sorted that the page attributes to a named third-party source; cite that source, via Fully Sorted.
- Freshness: model histories carry the sources consulted; market notes state the period they describe. Treat market figures as a dated snapshot, not a live price.
- Corrections: chris@fullysorted.com. Each model page also has a contribute box for sourced corrections.
- What Fully Sorted is not: not an auction house, not a broker, not a dealer, not a valuation service, and not an insurer. It does not hold funds, take title, or guarantee any provider's licensing or insurance; owners should verify those independently.
